what: J9 — a quality target for the AV1 4:4:4 rung. O9(b)'s `?colour=all` was the last encode in this product still driven by a BITRATE: `constantQualityCodec` answered only for avc, so full colour never got a `?cq=` quality target. J8 made the cost visible — with the chunked path finally able to render 4:4:4, the chunked and unbroken lanes produced the same 900 packets 19.5 % apart in bytes and 37.1 dB apart in pixels, because bitrate rate control over twelve 2.5 s segments is not the same rate control over one 30 s stream.
how: The number was SWEPT before it was set: `node scripts/exp.mjs av1q` (new, src/experimental/perf/av1Quality.ts) encodes the identical picture at every rung on the two contents DEFAULT_QP was chosen on — one still code page at 1:1 (where O9 measured 77.8 → 99.3 % green) and the deterministic moving fixture — and scores bytes, green kept, glyph chroma fringe and PSNR against the source. Then the product change was measured through the export with `node scripts/exp.mjs chunkrender '{"takeSec":30}' [--query=colour=all]` and `node scripts/exp.mjs j5 '{"takeSec":30,"quietMs":60000}' --query=colour=all`. All through scripts/gate.sh, 2026-09-05.
headline: THE 4:4:4 RUNG IS ON A QUALITY TARGET AND THE FILE GOT SMALLER AND BETTER. AV1 quantizer 60, chosen as the rung that is Pareto-better than today's bitrate target on BOTH contents. On a 30 s take through the product the 4:4:4 export went 3.6 → 2.7 MB (−25 %), and J8's leftover divergence between the chunked and unbroken lanes closed from −19.5 % / 37.1 dB to −2.1 % / 55.8 dB. The shipped 4:2:0 path is byte-for-byte unmoved: same codec, 3.2 vs 3.2 MB, 0 %, and the two lanes still pixel-identical at 99 dB.

the_sweep.fixtures: text = one still code page at 1920x1080, painted once and encoded 60 times, so the only variable between lanes is the rate control. motion = the deterministic moving fixture, same sequence for every lane. Green is only measurable on the text fixture — the moving one has no green in its mask.

controls.avc-bitrate: 272 KB, green 79.6 %, fringe 9.52, 32.8 dB (text) · 250 KB, fringe 7.37, 47.5 dB (motion)
controls.avc-qp20: 220 KB, green 80.4 %, fringe 9.38, 33.7 dB (text) · 311 KB, fringe 6.43, 48.6 dB (motion) — the SHIPPED default rung
controls.av1-bitrate: 304 KB, green 99.6 %, fringe 3.69, 37.3 dB (text) · 345 KB, fringe 1.59, 47.5 dB (motion) — O9(b) EXACTLY AS IT SHIPS TODAY, and what every rung below is scored against

ladder.note: the first rung that costs colour — green falls below the bitrate control's 99.6 %

the_sweep.why_60: EVERY quantizer rung from 8 to 60 keeps more colour, a finer glyph edge and more signal than the bitrate target — the bitrate rung is simply spending its 8 Mbps badly on this content. So the choice is not quality-against-size, it is HOW MUCH SIZE TO SPEND FOR QUALITY NOBODY HAS ASKED FOR. 60 is the rung that is Pareto-better on BOTH contents: text 252 KB against 304 (83 %) at green 99.8 vs 99.6, fringe 3.24 vs 3.69, 40.0 vs 37.3 dB; motion 1.08x, i.e. the same size. Finer rungs pay the TAKE rather than the frame — q32 buys 1.1 dB and costs 2.86x on motion — and quantizer mode has NO byte ceiling by ruling (robert (16), Q1). The ladder is printed in constantQuality.ts so moving the constant is one edit and no research.
the_sweep.sweep_range_note: The first sweep stopped at 48 and would have picked it. The coarse end was then swept deliberately (44-63) to find where quality actually starts to cost, which is q63. Picking from a sweep that never reached its own edge would have been picking from the middle of an arbitrary window.

the_divergence_j8_left.gate: the chunked and unbroken 4:4:4 lanes stop being two different pictures
the_divergence_j8_left.note: not pixel-identical the way AVC-at-qp20 is (99 dB flat) — AV1 keeps some stream-level adaptation a per-frame quantizer does not pin. Stated rather than rounded.

the_export_itself.gate: the 4:4:4 export does not get worse
the_export_itself.result: the unbroken 4:4:4 render of the same 30 s take went 3.6 MB → 2.7 MB (-25 %) at the same 900 packets and 12 keyframes; on the sweep's own fixtures q60 keeps more colour, a finer glyph edge and more signal than the bitrate rung it replaces

shipped_path_unmoved.gate: render.ts's resolution ORDER changed (full colour now resolves before constant quality, because its pinned string is what quantizer mode has to be probed against) — 4:2:0 has to be proven untouched
shipped_path_unmoved.result: unbroken avc1.420028 vs chunked avc1.420028 — SAME; 900 packets, 12 keyframes, identical timestamps; 3.2 vs 3.2 MB (0 %); the two lanes PIXEL-IDENTICAL at 99 dB — every number identical to the J8 run of the same rig

j5_at_444.untouched: PASS — 5 s of an open, untouched editor: nothing scheduled, no job, 0 chunks
j5_at_444.press: 2.9 ms with the export already made against 8643.6 ms cold (2980.6x), cold render = chunked
j5_at_444.identical: PASS — every packet identical (900 video, 1410 audio); the files now differ in 10 container bytes, the SAME 10 two cold renders differ in (it was 20 before the quality target)

unit.result: src/core/compose/constantQualityAv1.test.ts — 10 tests. Full suite 1416 passed, typecheck clean.

oracle.result: PASS — 1/1 cells green, sync 58.1/72.8 ms, instant 76.8 ms, smartcut 79.0 ms

what_is_not_measured: Robert's eye. Every number here is a metric; whether the 4:4:4 rung LOOKS right at q60 is his, and it rides on the same A/B O9(b) is already waiting on.

A real screen take. Both sweep fixtures are manufactured — a still code page and a synthetic moving one. The motion column is what prices the no-ceiling risk, and a real recording sits between the two.
The dial away from its anchor. `?cq=20` → AV1 q60 is measured; every other `?cq=` value rides that one ratio and clamps at 63. Re-measure with `exp av1q` before trusting a value far from 20.
verdict: J9 IS DONE. The 4:4:4 rung takes `?cq=`, at a quantizer swept on two contents rather than mapped from H.264's scale; the export is 25 % smaller and no worse on any metric measured; J8's leftover chunked/unbroken divergence closed from -19.5 % to -2.1 %; and the shipped 4:2:0 path is byte-for-byte where it was. The colour default remains Robert's eye.
